chief_complaint: Management of chronic kidney disease with hypertension and metabolic risk factors
history_of_present_illness: The 61-year-old male has a longstanding history of obesity, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis of the hip. In mid‑2021 he was diagnosed with stage 1 chronic kidney disease and diabetic kidney disease, though no diabetes diagnosis or laboratory values are recorded. Blood pressure is well controlled on low‑dose lisinopril and amlodipine. Lipids are treated with low‑intensity simvastatin, but recent lipid panels are unavailable. He uses naproxen for hip pain, which poses a nephrotoxic risk given his CKD. Recent encounters have been primarily wellness visits; the last recorded encounter was a dental radiograph in July 2022. Several key laboratory results (BMI, A1c, eGFR, cholesterol) are missing, and medication reconciliation flagged duplicate simvastatin entries.

clinical_impression: The patient presents with a metabolic‑vascular phenotype characterized by early diabetic kidney disease, well‑controlled hypertension on low‑dose agents, suboptimally managed dyslipidemia, and obesity. NSAID use for osteoarthritis poses additional renal risk. Key gaps include absent diabetes confirmation, missing renal and lipid labs, and duplicate statin entry. Priorities are confirming and treating diabetes, optimizing lipid control, reviewing NSAID safety, and updating essential laboratory monitoring.
